sub_graphs.title: Engine API: Execution Payload Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the lifecycle of execution payloads from creation request through validation to retrieval, as communicated between the consensus and execution layers

nodes.label: CL Requests Payload Build
nodes.description: Consensus layer calls engine_forkchoiceUpdated with payloadAttributes to initiate execution payload construction

nodes.label: Validate Forkchoice State
nodes.description: Execution layer validates headBlockHash references a known valid payload, safeBlockHash is ancestor of head, and finalizedBlockHash is consistent

nodes.label: Update Fork Choice Atomically
nodes.description: Atomically update the execution layer's canonical chain head, safe block, and finalized block references

nodes.label: Initiate Payload Build Process
nodes.description: Begin constructing an execution payload: start with empty transactions, continuously update from mempool, using provided timestamp, prevRandao, and suggestedFeeRecipient

nodes.label: Payload Under Construction
nodes.description: Execution payload is being continuously updated with transactions from the mempool; payloadId has been assigned

nodes.label: Retrieve Built Payload
nodes.description: CL calls engine_getPayload with payloadId to retrieve the most recent version of the constructed payload

nodes.label: Payload Delivered to CL
nodes.description: The execution payload has been returned to the consensus layer for inclusion in a beacon block

nodes.label: Validate New Payload
nodes.description: CL calls engine_newPayload with an ExecutionPayload; EL validates block hash, transactions, terminal conditions, and executes the block

nodes.label: Payload Validated as VALID
nodes.description: Execution payload passed all validation; status VALID returned with latestValidHash

nodes.label: Payload Validated as INVALID
nodes.description: Execution payload failed validation; status INVALID returned with latestValidHash pointing to last valid ancestor

nodes.label: Payload Status SYNCING
nodes.description: Required data for validation is unavailable; EL returns SYNCING and needs to sync from peers

edges.label: State is valid, update canonical chain
Fork choice updated, begin payload construction
Payload build started with payloadId assigned
Return latest payload version to CL
Payload passes all checks, return VALID

external_entities.name: Consensus Layer Client
external_entities.description: The beacon node that drives the execution layer via the Engine API JSON-RPC interface

sub_graphs.title: Engine API: Authentication and Trust Boundary
sub_graphs.description: Models the security boundary between consensus and execution layers, including JWT authentication and error handling

nodes.label: Engine API Request Received on Port 8551
nodes.description: An incoming JSON-RPC request arrives on the dedicated Engine API port (default 8551)

nodes.label: Authenticate JWT Token
nodes.description: Verify the JWT bearer token in the request header against the shared secret between CL and EL

nodes.label: Request Authenticated
nodes.description: JWT authentication passed, request is from an authorized consensus layer client

nodes.label: Authentication Failed
nodes.description: JWT verification failed; request is rejected

nodes.label: Exchange Capabilities
nodes.description: Process engine_exchangeCapabilities to discover mutually supported methods between CL and EL

nodes.label: Enforce Message Ordering
nodes.description: Process engine_forkchoiceUpdated calls sequentially in the order received to prevent race conditions

nodes.label: Request Processed
nodes.description: Engine API request has been authenticated, validated, and processed

edges.label: JSON-RPC request arrives on Engine API port

external_entities.name: Engine API Caller
external_entities.description: Any entity connecting to the Engine API port; should only be an authorized CL client but could be an attacker if JWT secret is compromised

sub_graphs.title: Engine API: Error Codes and Recovery
sub_graphs.description: Models the error handling states and recovery paths in the Engine API

nodes.label: Error: Unknown Payload (-38001)
nodes.description: engine_getPayload called with a payloadId that does not exist or has expired

nodes.label: Error: Invalid Forkchoice State (-38002)
nodes.description: engine_forkchoiceUpdated called with inconsistent block hash references (e.g., safe not ancestor of head)

nodes.label: Error: Invalid Payload Attributes (-38003)
nodes.description: payloadAttributes fail validation (e.g., timestamp not greater than head block timestamp)

nodes.label: Error: Too Large Request (-38004)
nodes.description: Request contains too many entities (excessive block range, etc.)

nodes.label: Error: Unsupported Fork (-38005)
nodes.description: Request references a fork version the EL does not recognize

nodes.label: CL Handles Error Response
nodes.description: Consensus layer processes the error code and determines recovery strategy: retry, adjust parameters, or alert operator

nodes.label: CL Retries Request
nodes.description: CL adjusts parameters and retries the Engine API call

ambiguities.text: The specification states the payload build process should 'continuously update' the transaction set from the mempool but does not define the update frequency or prioritization strategy.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations use their own transaction ordering heuristics (typically gas price priority). The continuous update runs until getPayload is called or 12 seconds elapse.

ambiguities.text: The ACCEPTED status means 'structurally sound but not yet fully validated' - the conditions under which a payload transitions from ACCEPTED to VALID or INVALID are not fully specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume ACCEPTED is returned for payloads on side branches that pass structural checks; full validation occurs when/if the CL makes them canonical via forkchoiceUpdated.

ambiguities.text: In one-to-many load-balancing configurations, the spec does not define conflict resolution when multiple ELs return different validation results for the same payload.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the CL treats any INVALID response as authoritative and raises an alert. Multiple VALID responses are expected to be consistent.

implicit_assumptions.description: The JWT shared secret between CL and EL is assumed to be securely generated, stored, and not accessible to unauthorized parties.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: An attacker with the JWT secret could send arbitrary Engine API calls to the EL, potentially manipulating fork choice, injecting invalid payloads, or causing denial of service.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Engine API communication between CL and EL is assumed to occur over localhost or a trusted network, not exposed to the public internet.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Network-level attackers could intercept or replay Engine API calls, even with JWT auth, potentially through man-in-the-middle attacks if TLS is not used.

implicit_assumptions.description: It is assumed that only one CL client writes fork choice updates to each EL in a one-to-many configuration.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Multiple CLs sending conflicting forkchoiceUpdated calls would cause the EL to oscillate between chain heads, potentially leading to inconsistent state.
